```{r set-options, echo=FALSE,message=FALSE}
options(width=120)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(fig.width=12,fig.height=8,fig.align='center')
library(printr) # to print library(help=...)
```


Sometimes, when we want to visualise something unusual, 
we may need to use very low-level tools.

As an example, let's take the positions of planets of the Solar System with respect to Earth on 11 November 2026, 14:00 GMT,
from http://cosinekitty.com/solar_system.html: 
```{r planets-print}
print(planets <- read.csv("planets2026.csv"))
```   
The distances and coordinates are in astronomical units (1AU = 149 597 870 700 m, or the mean distance between Earth and Sun).
The unit for the radii is the radius of Earth.


Let's start with a minimal plot:
```{r plot-minimal}
plot.new()
plot.window(xlim=c(0,1),ylim=c(0,1))
plot.xy(xy.coords(x=0.5,y=0.5),type="p")
```   

Higher-level functions have a lot of defaults:
```{r plot-default}
plot.default(planets$X)
```   

We need to look at the data and decide what we want to plot:
```{r planets-summary}
summary(planets)
```   
The Z coordinate seems less informative in comparison, so we will ignore it instead of choosing some 
more complicated projection.

Prepare the canvas using some mid-level graphics (here `plot` is the same as `plot.default`): 
```{r plot-boundaries}
xrange <- range(planets$X)
yrange <- range(planets$Y)
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU")
```   

Not quite square! We need to set a graphical parameter:
```{r plot-square}
par(pty="s")
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1)
```   

Some extra change:
```{r plot-las}
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
# las=1 write labels on the vertical axis horizonally
```   

Now we can add the points for planets:
```{r planets-points}
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
points(planets$X,planets$Y) 
```

The points are unrecognisable. Let's add some visual attributes: 
the colours are approximately the real colours of the planets, 
the shapes emphasise the most important planets, Sun and Earth,
and the point sizes are proportional to the planet radii in the *logarithmic scale*.
```{r planets-symbols}
planet.colours <- c("orange","black","brown","deepskyblue","red","tan","gold","cyan","blue")
planet.shapes <- c(8,16,16,10,16,16,16,16,16)
planet.sizes <- round(log(planets$Radius + 2)*0.8,1)
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
points(planets$X,planets$Y,
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes) 
```   

Add a legend and title:
```{r planets-legend}
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
points(planets$X,planets$Y,
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes) 

# title 
title.bottom <- mean(yrange)+0.5*(xrange[2]-xrange[1])-1
text(x=-xrange[1]-9,y=title.bottom,
     labels="Planets of the Solar System",adj=0,cex=2.8,col="red")

# legend
legend.right <- xrange[2] - 0.5
rect(xleft = legend.right - 7.5, ybottom = title.bottom - 4 - nrow(planets),
     xright = legend.right, ytop = title.bottom - 2.5)
points(x=rep(legend.right-5.5,nrow(planets)),y=title.bottom - 3 - (1:nrow(planets)),
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes)
text(x=rep(legend.right-4,nrow(planets)),y=title.bottom - 3 - (1:nrow(planets)),
     labels=planets$Name,adj=0)
```   
The positions of the title and legend were found experimentally.

We can also save the picture as a pdf file:
```{r planets-pdf}
pdf("planets.pdf",width=9,height=9)
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=xrange,ylim=yrange,xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
points(planets$X,planets$Y,
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes) 

# title 
title.bottom <- mean(yrange)+0.5*(xrange[2]-xrange[1])-1
text(x=-xrange[1]-2,y=title.bottom,
     labels="Planets of the Solar System",adj=0,cex=2.8,col="red")

# legend
legend.right <- xrange[2] - 0.5
rect(xleft = legend.right - 7.5, ybottom = title.bottom - 4 - nrow(planets),
     xright = legend.right, ytop = title.bottom - 2.5)
points(x=rep(legend.right-5.5,nrow(planets)),y=title.bottom - 3 - (1:nrow(planets)),
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes)
text(x=rep(legend.right-4,nrow(planets)),y=title.bottom - 3 - (1:nrow(planets)),
     labels=planets$Name,adj=0)
dev.off()
```   

Low-level graphics require a lot of manual adjustments, and it is quite inconvenient if you need to change something.
For example, several years ago I decided to show 9 planets instead of 7 I showed the year before. 
Compare the code above with the following code and notice how many tweaks of 
graphical coordinates were necessary:
```{r planets-2021, eval=FALSE}
planets <- read.csv("planets2021.csv")
par(pty="s") 
plot(x=NULL,xlim=c(-10,10),ylim=c(-10,10),xlab="X, AU",ylab="Y, AU",asp=1,las=1)
points(planets$X,planets$Y,
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes) 
points(x=rep(7,nrow(planets)),y=9:3,
       col = planet.colours,
       pch = planet.shapes,
       cex = planet.sizes)
text(x=rep(8,nrow(planets)),y=9:3,labels=planets$Name,adj=0)
rect(xleft=5,ybottom=2,xright=10.5,ytop=10)
text(x=-10,y=9,labels="Planets of",adj=0,cex=3,col="red")
text(x=-10,y=7,labels="the Solar System",adj=0,cex=3,col="red")
```   


### Optional Exercise

Use low-level R graphics to draw a clock similar to the picture:

```{r clock,echo=FALSE}
hours <- 1:12 # the number of hours on the clock
a <- pi/2 - (2*pi/length(hours))*hours # vector of angles, in radians
x <- cos(a) # x coordinate on a unit circle
y <- sin(a) # y coordinate on a unit circle
plot.new() # create a clear plot
plot.window(x=NULL,xlim=c(-1,1),ylim=c(-1,1),asp=1) # set the coordinate system
plotrix::draw.circle(0,0,1,border="tomato",col="white") # draw a circle representing the face
points (0.7*x,0.7*y,pch=16,col="blue",cex=1.5) # put the blue points on a smaller circle
text (0.85*x,0.85*y,1:12,cex=2) # put the labels on a larger circle
h <- 10 # set hours
m <- 10 # set minutes
# alternatively, get the current hour and minute:
# h <- as.integer(format(Sys.time(),"%H"))
# m <- as.integer(format(Sys.time(),"%M"))
am <- pi/2 - (2*pi/60)*m # the angle of minute hand
arrows(0,0,0.6*cos(am) ,0.6*sin(am),col="green",lwd=2,angle=20) # plot minute hand
ah <- pi/2 - (2*pi/length(hours))*h # the angle of hour hand
ah <- ah - (2*pi/length(hours))*m/60 # to adjust the hour hand for each minute passed
arrows(0,0,0.4*cos(ah) ,0.4*sin(ah),col="yellow",lwd=4,angle=30) # plot hour hand
```   

You may find functions `arrows()` and `plotrix::draw.circle()` helpful.

Then use functions `Sys.time()` and `format()` to show the current time in your clock.
